messages:
martha: customer raised a 422 when calling /v1/rerank — they say scores are all 0 and some docs missing. quick glance shows payload has both "documents" and "candidates", plus a nested "query" inside each doc. can someone sanity-check if our parsing prefers root query vs doc.query?

martha: here's redacted snippet they sent:
```json
{
  "query": "best onboarding guide",           // root-level query
  "documents": [
    { "id": "d1", "text": "...", "query": "override text" },
    { "id": "d2", "text": "...", "passages": [{"id":"p1","text":"...","query":"passage q"}] }
  ],
  "candidates": [
    { "id": "c1", "text": "..." }
  ]
}
```

martha: they say expected behavior: root.query should be used for ranking, not per-doc query fields. but results show weird low scores and a 422 in some cases.

izzy: this looks like the qname shadowing we've seen once before — internal selector prefers the nearest "query" key (document-level) which can null out features when not in expected shape. can you paste exact error body from the API?

martha: error body is short: "422 Unprocessable Entity: malformed candidate mapping". response includes: "missing candidate_text for candidate id c1" even though candidate has text.

samir: that smells like our request shaping layer is flattening and de-duping keys. if a document has a nested query object or passages array with different shapes we sometimes drop candidate fields during validation. possible repro: if document.passages exists and we also send candidates it trips the candidate extractor.

izzy: digging into the parsing logic — we have a legacy branch that normalizes input by mapping any array-like things into an internal "items" list. if both "documents" and "candidates" present, we try to map candidates by id into docs, and if ids collide we drop text to avoid duplication. bug: the dedupe uses shallow key check and misses candidate_text when candidate lacks explicit "text" key (e.g., "content").

martha: customer says they definitely have "text" but SDK may have renamed it. can you check SDK v2 mapping?

izzy: confirm: SDK v2 has a mapping that will rename "text" to "content" in some helper flows. that would explain missing candidate_text leading to 422. so two root causes: (1) key rename in SDK v2; (2) parser dedupe that favors doc-side keys and nukes candidate.text when id matches.

kyle: next steps? customer impact is high (production traffic failing).

samir: immediate mitigation: server-side tolerance — treat candidate entries missing "text" as invalid only if we also can't find fallback in the blob; but better: fallback to root-level "query" and avoid dedupe that drops text. i'll open an emergency fix PR to stop dropping candidate.text when candidates present.

izzy: i'll add a quick validation change to prefer root.query if doc-specific query is present but empty string — but need to be careful not to break valid use cases where doc.query should override. propose: rule: root.query > doc.query unless request has explicit "use_document_query": true.

martha: good. i'll message customer with repro & temporary workaround: downgrade SDK to v1 OR ensure candidate entries include explicit "text" and remove nested per-doc "query" keys. share the exact repro steps?

martha: message drafted to customer: "short-term: please remove nested 'query' fields inside documents or include explicit 'text' on each candidate. we'll push a fix server-side to handle mixed payloads. ETA ~4 hours for a validation hotfix; SDK team will follow up about mapping change." will send after engineering confirms.

kyle: also log a docs note: call out that nested query names can shadow root query and SDK renames can break candidate text.

support-bot: Created issue CS-4921: "rerank: mixed documents+candidates + SDK v2 mapping -> missing candidate_text causing 422" assigned to samir, izzy. Priority: P0.

samir: linking PR #1428 (hotfix) here once CI passes. I'll call out possible regression tests.

izzy: I will add a small unit test checking: root.query present + doc.query present + use_document_query false -> use root.query. and test candidate.text fallback when SDK renamed key.

martha: thanks team — i'll update customer after PR merge. keeping thread open for rollback notes. :thumbsup:
